answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate plus incumbent's refusal to negotiate leaves no path through renegotiation (memory_c4 precedent shows this requires vendor willingness). The low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate—memory_c2 documents successful prior migration with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, reducing switch risk. However, assembly line running at 94% utilization creates delivery risk exposure. Verifying memory_c2 confirms onboarding speed and operational stability are achievable. The 14-day renewal window and single sourcing capacity force immediate decision. Switching to the low-cost vendor is operationally feasible based on prior success and financially necessary. The delivery buffer erosion is the real risk, but deferral sacrifices the mandate and forces a worse vendor squeeze next cycle. A standard experiment (phased volume migration over first 30 days) balances cost achievement against the thin operational margin.
